'''Shiomi no Sukune''' (塩海足尼, also rendered as Shibumi no Sukune or Shiomi no Sukune)<ref>[http://sakaorinomiya.jp/s/top.html Official Website of Sakaorimiya Shrine]</ref> was a prominent {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} noble and the first '''{{ill|Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|甲斐国造}}''' (Governor of Kai Province).

== Overview ==

In the {{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, Shiomi no Sukune is identified as a descendant of {{ill|Sahohiko no Mikoto|ja|狭穂彦王}}, suggesting a connection with the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏}}.

According to the traditions of {{ill|Sakaori-no-Miya|ja|酒折宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakaorimiya Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11644327}}, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|倭建命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} visited Kai Province, he entrusted Shiomi no Sukune with a sacred flint pouch, saying, "May my spirit remain here and be venerated." Shiomi no Sukune established a shrine on the slopes of Tsukimi Mountain, enshrining the flint as the deity. Scholars such as Masayoshi Isogai and Hidesaburō Hara associate the "Elder of Sacred Fires" mentioned in the legends with Shiomi no Sukune.<ref name="#1">Hara, Hidesaburō. "Paths to the East and Royal Authority," in *Ancient Japan Volume 7: Chubu*, Kadokawa Shoten, 1993.</ref>

Shiomi no Sukune appears in the founding legends of numerous historic shrines in Kai Province. For example:
- {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社|lt=Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki)}} is said to have originated when he enshrined the deity {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}} from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|abstract|Q705542|ar|معبد أوميوا|fa|معبد اومیوا|fr|Ōmiwa-jinja|id|Kuil Ōmiwa|ja|大神神社|la|Templum Ōmiwa|my|အိုးမိဝကျောင်းတော်|ru|Оомива-дзиндзя|simple|Ōmiwa Shrine|tok|tomo sewi Omiwa|zh|大神神社|qid=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in the Keikō era.
- {{ill|Kanazakura Shrine|ja|金櫻神社}} traces its roots to Shiomi no Sukune's construction of a hall for Yamato Takeru's worship in the 40th year of Emperor Keikō's reign.
- {{ill|Shizuoka Sengen Shrine|ja|神部神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinbu Shrine (Yamanashi)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 静岡浅間神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q500368}} attributes its founding to Shiomi no Sukune bringing a deity from Mount Hiei in {{ill|Ōmi Province|ca|Província d'Ōmi|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆمی|cs|Provincie Ómi|de|Provinz Ōmi|es|Provincia de Ōmi|fa|ولایت اومی|fi|Ōmin provinssi|fr|Province d'Ōmi|gl|Provincia de Ōmi|hak|Ōmi-koet|id|Provinsi Ōmi|it|Ōmi|ja|近江国|ko|오미국|lt|Omio žemė|nl|Omi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Ōmi|pt|Província de Ōmi|ru|Оми (провинция)|simple|Ōmi Province|sk|Ómi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оми|tr|Ōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Омі|vi|Tỉnh Ōmi|zh|近江國|zh_min_nan|Ômi-kok|zh_yue|近江國|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi Province}}.
- Nakamaki Shrine was established by Shiomi no Sukune at Emperor Keikō's command after Yamato Takeru's visit to Sakaorimiya Shrine.

Beyond shrines, Shiomi no Sukune is also central to the foundation myth of {{ill|Shimobe Spa|ja|下部温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimobe Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11361358}}, which recounts his discovery of the hot springs during a regional inspection.<ref>Japan Spa Association, "[https://www.spa.or.jp/kokumin/971/ Shimobe Onsen]."</ref>

Shiomi no Sukune is enshrined as a deity at {{ill|Kokuritsu Shrine|ja|国立神社}}.

== Genealogy ==

Shiomi no Sukune was the child of Chitohiko no Mikoto, the great-grandson of {{ill|Sahohiko no Mikoto|ja|狭穂彦王}}.
